title: Countdown to Kickoff: Spencer Rattler is the Saints Player of Day 2
description: Spencer Rattler goes into his third NFL season, now as the New Orleans Saints backup QB behind Tyler Shough. He's our Saints Player of the Day.
fullText:
Friday means a mere two days before the New Orleans Saints' 2026 regular season opener. The Saints will play at the Detroit Lions to start off their year on Sunday, Sept. 13. Quarterback Spencer Rattler wears No. 2 for New Orleans as he enters his third season. Rattler is our most recent Saints Player of the Day feature.

Name (age): Spencer Rattler (25)

Height, weight: 6-foot, 211 pounds

College: South Carolina Gamecocks

Drafted: Round 5, 150 overall in 2024

2026 salary cap hit: $1.16 million

A five-star prospect from Pinnacle High School, Rattler was a prominent national recruit who decided on the Oklahoma Sooners. He played sparingly as a true freshman in 2019 before winning the starting job the following year. Rattler led the Big 12 in completion percentage (67.5%), passing yards (3,031) and touchdowns (28) while guiding the Sooners to a 9-2 mark and earning 1st Team All-Big 12 honors. Entering 2021 as a Heisman Trophy favorite, Rattler was statistically solid but uneven play led to him getting benched in favor of Caleb Williams. He'd transfer to South Carolina at the season's conclusion.

Rattler quarterbacked the Gamecocks for his final two years of eligibility, leading them to a 13-12 overall mark. In those two seasons, he threw for 6,212 yards with 37 touchdowns, 20 interceptions, and a 67.5% completion percentage. Rattler's collegiate career ended with a 68.5% completion rate, 10,807 passing yards, 77 touchdowns, and 32 interceptions.

After six quarterbacks were picked in the first round of the 2024 NFL draft, their wasn't another signal caller chosen until the Saints grabbed Rattler in Round 5 with the 150th overall selection. He was expected to learn and develop behind starter Derek Carr for his first season. That all changed when Carr went down with an injury in Week 5. Rattler got his first career start in Week 6 against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, playing well in spurts during a blowout loss. He'd start the next two games with worsening results until getting benched for Jake Haener against the Chargers. Carr returned the following week, but lasted just five games before going down again with a season-ending injury.

After Carr's second injury, the Saints turned to Haener to start against Washington. That experiment lasted only a half, as Rattler took over and played arguably his best game of the year. Those results didn't carry over, as Rattler started the year's last three games but really only played reasonably well in a season finale rematch against Tampa Bay. An albeit injury-depleted Saints team lost all seven of Rattler's game appearances, averaging just 13.3 points in the process. Rattler completed 57% of his throws for 1,317 yards with 4 touchdowns and 5 interceptions while taking 22 sacks.

Under new head coach Kellen Moore and an entirely new coaching staff in 2025, Rattler competed with second-round rookie draft choice Tyler Shough for the starting job in preseason. It was an even competition, but Rattler was given the opportunity to start the year. That lasted eight games before the Saints turned to Shough to start the remaining nine contests. Under Rattler, New Orleans averaged a meager 15.1 points per outing with Rattler averaging 198.3 passing yards per game and an abysmal 6.2 per attempt.

Spencer Rattler held off Zach Wilson for the backup job during the 2026 offseason. However, neither showed little to inspire confidence if they have to step in for Shough. Given his experience in the system, Rattler should be the favorite to back up Shough this season.

title: The Wolf deals again for the Mud Hens
description: Scores, news, and notes from around the Detroit Tigers’ farm system for Thursday, September 10, 2026.
fullText:
Once again, left-hander Jackson Wolf delivered for the Mud Hens on Thursday night. He tossed five innings of one-run ball, allowing just two hits and three walks, striking out five.

His teammates took advantage in the top of the third. Justice Bigbie led off with a single and eventually scored on a Cal Stevenson triple with two outs. Max Anderson struck out, but it was 1-0 lead for the Hens.

In the fourth, Jace Jung singled with one out and rode home on a Carlos Pérez homer to make it 3-0.

Carlos Perez crushes a 2-run homer 457 feet to left to give Toledo a 3-0 lead. Perez now has 7 home runs in 7 games with the Mud Hens. pic.twitter.com/GL6zTHn7Eo

A pair of singles and a wild pitch from Wolf led to a run in the bottom of the fourth, but that was all he'd allow.

They got that run right back in the fifth. Max Burt singled and stole second with one out. Another triple from Stevenson scored him to make it 4-1 Hens. This time, Anderson singled him in to make it 5-1.

Enmanuel de Jesus took over for a scoreless sixth. He got in a spot of bother in the seventh, but Hayden Minton shut that down to send this to the eighth.

Singles from Corey Julks and Jace Jung were followed by a walk to Bennett Lee to load the bases with no outs in the top of the eighth. The Cubs then walked James Oatman to force in a run. Justice Bigbie then ripped a double, scoring Jung, but Lee was thrown out at home, and Outman was caught trying to score and tagged out as well. So only one run scored, but Michael Siani then blasted a two-run shot to right field, and it was 9-1 Hens.

Minton handled the eighth without much trouble, though his velocity, which has peaked up to 95-96 mph in relief, was down in the 92 mph range.

In the top of the ninth, Julks walked and Lee was hit by a pitch with two outs, but Outman struck out.

Tyler Mattison took over from Minton and closed it out, though it's worth nothing that his velocity, already well off the 95-96 mph he used to have, has fallen all the way down to 91-92 mph.

Stevenson: 2-5, R, 2 RBI, 2 3B, K

Wolf: 5.0 IP, ER, 2 H, 3 BB, 5 K

Coming Up Next: It's an 8:08 p.m. ET start time on Friday night in Des Moines.

Kenny Serwa was mauled badly in this one, though the SeaWolves piled up plenty of offense of their own. In the process, they established a new team Eastern League stolen base record, with 273 and counting.

The 29-year-old knuckleballer doesn't strike out many, and this time the balls in play were finding the grass. He gave up four in the second, single runs in the third and fifth, and then one more before departing in the sixth.

The SeaWolves got a quick run when Woody Hadeen led off the game with a single, stole second, and scored on an E.J. Exposito single. Finally, in the fifth they broke through again. Viandel Pena drew a leadoff walk but was forced by a Woody Hadeen grounder. Zyhir Hope singled through the right side, and he and Hadeen pulled off the double steal. Hadeen scored on an E.J. Exposito ground out.

At that point it was 5-2 Reading, but three straight hits off of Serwa started the fifth, producing a 6-2 lead.

In the top of the sixth, Luke Shliger stayed hot with a leadoff double. Roberto Campos drove a two-run shot the opposite way to pull Erie within two runs. Seth Stephenson followed that blast with a single and a stolen base. Pena doubled him in and later scored on a balk to tie the game.

Roberto Campos shoots a 2-run homer to right center to pull Erie back within two run. It’s his first home run of the season. pic.twitter.com/Xx3pv2HcFH

Serwa gave up a one-out walk in the sixth and was replaced by Eric Silva, who crumbled, allowing three runs to score for a 9-6 Reading lead.

Izaac Pacheco launched his 21st homer of the season in the seventh.

Izaac Pacheco smashes the first pitch of the 7th inning for his 24th home run of the season. Erie still trails 9-7. pic.twitter.com/pOcgurzbnR

Unfortunately Johan Simon was wild in the eighth, and eventually allowed a two run single to make it 11-7 Reading. Chris Meyers and Pacheco walked to start the top of the ninth. Campos came through again with a one-out double to score both runs. So it was 11-9 Reading, and there was still only one out in the inning. The bullpen was cracking. A wild pitch got Campos to third, and an error on a Stephenson ground ball scored him to make it 11-10 Reading. But right there, with victory within reach, Pena grounded into a game ending double play.

Stephenson: 3-5, R, RBI, 2B, SB

Pacheco: 1-4, 2 R, RBI, HR, BB, 2 K

Serwa (L, 9-9): 5.1 IP, 7 ER, 9 H, 4 BB, K

title: One year until first women's Lions Test - will it be a success?
description: With the first British and Irish Lions women's Test 12 months away, BBC Sport looks at how preparations are going and whether the tour will be a success.
fullText:
Sporting history will be made one year from today when the first British and Irish Lions women's team runs out at Auckland's Go Media Stadium.

They will be taking on six-time world champions New Zealand on 11 September 2027 in the first of a three-Test series.

Lions chief executive Ben Calveley says the month-long tour, which was announced in 2024, will be a "hugely significant" milestone and "something truly special for the women's game".

New Zealand Rugby says it is "hugely excited about what's ahead", describing the tour as a "significant moment for rugby globally and a fantastic opportunity for New Zealand to get behind the Black Ferns and some of the world's best players".

And for the individuals chosen to pull on the famous red jersey, it will no doubt be the pinnacle of their rugby careers.

So with the countdown now truly on, BBC Sport takes a look at how preparations are going and if the tour is likely to be a first-time triumph or a live case study for the future.

The fixture dates, opposition, cities and host venues were all announced at the start of this year.

The Lions start their tour in the North Island city of Whangarei before travelling down to Auckland for the first Test.

There has been some disappointment expressed that the city's iconic Eden Park was not chosen as a venue after it hosted the 2022 Rugby World Cup final.

A mid-week fixture follows in Hamilton, before the tour heads to the South Island for the second and third Tests in Wellington and Christchurch.

4 Sept, Whangarei, Semenoff Stadium, v Black Ferns XV

11 Sept, first Test - Auckland, Go Media Stadium, v Black Ferns

14 Sept, Hamilton, FMG Stadium Waikato, v Invitational XV

18 Sept, second Test - Wellington, Sky Stadium, v Black Ferns

25 Sept, third Test - Christchurch, One NZ Stadium, v Black Ferns

We also know that former England captain Jo Yapp will be the Lions head coach.

She stated from the off that there will be no token selections and will pick the best players possible - which suggests the squad will have a significant England contingent.

Yapp makes history as first Lions Women coach

Lions coach Yapp wants elite players on NZ tour

It remains to be seen who Yapp will select for her backroom staff, but appointments will have to be made sooner rather than later given the impact it could have on the home nations' coaching teams prior to the 2027 Women's Six Nations.

It is understood that conversations are happening now as a priority.

Naturally, speculation has already begun, with Rachel Taylor, Sarah Hunter, Emily Scarratt, Giselle Mather and Susie Appleby among the potential candidates.

The player squad will be announced in May after the Six Nations. Whether that will be a 38-strong squad like the men's in 2025 remains to be seen.

There is also the question of who will be given the honour of captaining the team, with England's Meg Jones a clear front-runner.

A pre-tour fixture in the UK was mentioned earlier this year, and while we understand that is still going ahead, details are yet to be announced.

Alice Soper, New Zealand rugby journalist and co-host of the Full Credit podcast, says if you ask a random person on the street they would probably be unaware the Lions women are coming next year.

Apart from some marketing worked into Black Ferns communications, she said "it's been quiet", with women's sports coverage on the decline since the 2022 Rugby World Cup.

"In rugby terms, they [New Zealand Rugby] knocked-on what should have been an easy try. There were so many things they missed to be able to continue that momentum," Soper said.

She also points to poor timing, with the women's domestic leagues having already wrapped up and the small matter of what is happening in Australia a month later.

"The real risk is this tour being lost in the noise," Soper said.

"It's taking place just before the men's Rugby World Cup just across the ditch in Aussie, so the coverage will be wall-to-wall All Blacks at that stage.

"It's a real test for the strength of the home nation's fanbase. The success of this series will rest on them making the trip to Aotearoa to bring the hype. They bring that full energy and it may just be infectious enough to spur the locals into action."

British and Irish Lions marketing says "more than 124,000 supporters are expected to enjoy the action in person".

Tickets go on sale at the end of this month, while packages ranging from £1,595 to £14,495 are already available.

There is a worry though that stadia will struggle to sell out, with the Black Ferns' recent attendances languishing around 6,000-10,000.

But recent signs show there is cause for optimism.

The new One NZ Stadium in Christchurch, the third Test venue, is proving a real draw and has worked hard to build a women's rugby fan base.

As a result, 11,793 turned out to watch Matatu take on Chiefs Manawa in June's season opener

"New Zealand Rugby has had to start building this audience from scratch," explained Soper. "They are slowly getting there."

Super Rugby Aupiki operated as a fully professional, full-time competition for the first time this year and with firmer pathways now in place, the Black Ferns appear to be, what Soper calls "a team that is here to stay rather than sporadically assembled".

The new WXV Global Series will no doubt provide an easy platform to drum up interest for the Lions tour.

As luck would have it, the Black Ferns will be in the UK later this month for Tests against Scotland and England, before hosting France in three of the Lions' venues in October.

It should at the very least spark up some conversations while we await further announcements.

And for the players and coaches, it is a time to put their hand up for selection and become part of what will be sporting history.

title: Prop Vunipola set to retire before Leicester move
description: Former England prop Mako Vunipola was planning to retire as a player before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind.
fullText:
Former England prop Mako Vunipola says he was planning to retire before a phone call from from Leicester Tigers head coach Geoff Parling changed his mind.

The 35-year-old ex-Saracens front-rower, who won four Premiership titles and and the European Champions Cup three times with the London club, has moved back to England's top flight after two years in France with Vannes to play under former international team-mate Parling.

The pair featured for England together more than a decade ago and were also part of the British and Irish Lions team that toured Australia in 2013.

Vunipola said it was "pretty random" how he was convinced to make a U-turn on his decision to hang up his boots and join a Leicester side that Parling guided to the Prem semi-finals in his first season at the helm.

"I was pretty set on retiring last year, finishing my time in France," Vunipola told BBC East Midlands Today.

"Then in January I had a conversation with Geoff, he rang me and we spoke about this season and he asked me the question if I'd like to come and see if I can add value here at Leicester.

"The conversation I had with Geoff were really positive, and not just myself but for my family as well. My wife was a big part of the decision to come back to England

"Having these conversations with Geoff, we both felt really good about the club he is building here and obviously I knew Leicester had such a good history anyway."

Ex-England prop Vunipola among four Leicester signings

Listen to the Tigers Rugby Show on BBC Radio Leicester

Parling said Vunipola not only adds vast experience to the Tigers, but also a calming voice to a pack that lost Wales loose-head prop Niki Smith to Sale Sharks and back row Hanro Liebenberg, who decided to return to South Africa with the Bulls.

With decorated front rower Vunipola now committed to playing beyond his 36th birthday, Parling says managing the physical demands put on the summer's high-profile recruit will be vital.

"Am I going to expect him to play six games on the trot, no. And he knows that," Parling said.

"But when he's in, he rips in and he has been brilliant so far - he is working hard and he has been a positive influence."

Vunipola says the job he has at Tigers, and the way he intends to distinguish himself as a leader with the East Midlands club, is to "be as good as I can be".

"I can do all the talking I want off the field, but I have to make sure I play well and add value on the field to help this team," Vunipola said.

And as he prepares for his first Prem campaign in two years, he was asked if his return to the English game might also lead to him rethinking his place in the international arena.

Before he left for France he retired from England duties, but could that door be opened again to add to the 79 caps he won between 2012 and 2023?

"I got way too much work to do before I get anywhere near that," Vunipola said with a smile.

"I just have to be here and be a player for Leicester first and foremost. But no, nothing of that sort is in my mind.

"And if they get to that point where they are calling me, there must be something wrong going on."

title: Just like riding a bike - five things to watch in the EFL
description: BBC Sport looks at five key talking points before the weekend's Championship, League One and League Two action.
fullText:
"You stay upright and move forward so long as you keep up the momentum."

Former UN Secretary General Ban Ki-moon might not have been talking specifically about the English Football League when he produced that quote, but he's right, success, or failure, in the EFL is just like riding a bike.

Plenty of teams across the 72 have already found their rhythm in the early stages of this campaign but others are seemingly in desperate need of stabilisers.

We have picked out five things to look out for in this weekend's fixtures in the Championship, League One and League Two, including some fascinating reunions with former clubs for some coaches.

West Brom were wobbling all over the place when James Morrison hopped into the saddle in interim charge at The Hawthorns in February.

Albion were second-bottom of the Championship on 11 March but a 10-match unbeaten streak kept them up and, six games into the new season, the Baggies are top of the league.

Wednesday's 1-0 win at Derby - in which Albion played with 10 men for over an hour to secure just a second win at the Rams in 107 years - showcased their change in momentum. It was a ninth clean sheet in 18 league games under Morrison.

They face a stern test of their credentials as QPR head to the West Midlands on Saturday (12:30 BST).

The Hoops, like Albion, have lost only once this season, with that defeat coming against Middlesbrough, and are two points behind the pace-setters in a congested chasing pack.

Julien Stephan's side took just 11 points from their final 13 matches of last season, losing eight of them to finish in 15th, but a summer overhaul seems to have shifted their momentum, despite a mounting injury list.

Three years can seem a lifetime in football.

At the start of October 2023, John Eustace was Birmingham boss, with his side sixth in the Championship, having guided the turbulent Blues to a 17th-place finish in his first season at St Andrew's.

He was then controversially sacked by City's new American owners to make way for Wayne Rooney.

Eustace enjoyed a successful spell at Blackburn before making the switch to Derby, steering the Rams away from trouble at the end of 2024-25 before making a late run at the play-offs last season.

Wednesday's dismal 1-0 home defeat by 10-man West Brom was a fourth in their opening six games and the natives have become a little restless, despite a troublesome injury list and a failed takeover on the eve of the new campaign.

On Saturday, Eustace welcomes his former club to Pride Park (12:30 BST) with pressure also growing on Chris Davies, who has just started his third campaign in charge at St Andrew's.

Davies took Blues straight back up from League One in record-breaking fashion in his first season at the helm, but expectations have risen, along with the budget, and although they lost for the first time at Norwich on Wednesday, seven points from six matches is an underwhelming return.

A repeat of last season's 1-0 home win for the Rams would make things feel far rosier for Eustace, but far less so for Davies.

While West Brom are sitting pretty at the top of the Championship, one of the sides who fell short in last season's survival battle were Leicester.

The Foxes are now languishing in 18th in League One, with just five points from their opening five games.

They are already seven points behind leaders Sheffield Wednesday, who won just two games in the Championship last season albeit under exceptional circumstances, and lost their last game 4-0 at home against the other side to come down, Oxford United.

The momentum at the King Power is firmly downwards, but it has to change at some point, right?

On Saturday they travel to Stockport (15:00 BST).

When the Foxes were enjoying their finest hour, winning the Premier League in 2015-16, the Hatters finished ninth in National League North - 125 places below.

Five years ago, when Leicester last played in Europe and finished eighth in the Premier League, County were in the National League.

Both clubs are under new stewardship this season, but Jimmy McNulty has Stockport 15 places higher than Russell Martin's men and Hatters fans will be hoping to continue that momentum in the first league meeting between the sides in 18 seasons.

If you're looking into how momentum changes, then Hillsborough at the start of May, is a good place to start.

The announcement of the takeover of Sheffield Wednesday by a US consortium came moments before the Owls picked up their first win in over seven months - a span of 40 games - beating West Brom on the final day of the 2025-26 season.

Wednesday had suffered the earliest ever relegation in EFL history in February, with 13 Championship games remaining, but they have started with a bang this time around.

Four wins in five games has them top of the pile, with an EFL Cup win over Championship Bolton also highlighting how the tide has turned.

They welcome struggling Wigan Athletic on Saturday (15:00 BST).

After ending last season with one point and no goals in their final three games, the momentum has bled into this season too, the Latics have lost four of their five games so far in League One, plus their EFL Cup tie on penalties.

Gary Caldwell's side have failed to score in three of their past four and the 4-0 home drubbing by local rivals Stockport last time out saw them fall to the bottom of the table on goal difference.

It feels like a case of unstoppable force versus movable object unless Wigan can show they are up for the fight.

Always nice to meet up with some old faces, isn't it?

Scott Lindsey has the opportunity to do just that as his old team Swindon head to York City on Saturday (15:00 BST).

Lindsey spent two years coaching the Robins' under-18s a decade ago before returning to the club in 2021 as Ben Garner's assistant, then taking the big job himself the following summer after Garner's departure for Charlton.

It lasted just six months, he left in January with promotion-chasing Town sitting outside the play-offs on goal difference, to join Crawley, who were 21st in the same division and he later told the press he felt he never had the backing of Swindon fans.

Lindsey was parachuted in as York boss on the eve of the season after the shock departure of Stuart Maynard and has led the Minstermen to eight points from their opening five games, meaning they could leapfrog second-placed Swindon with a win, while the Robins could go top if they can pick up three points.

BBC Sport will have live text coverage of all the weekend's EFL action, starting with West Ham v Wrexham on Friday, throughout Saturday's fixtures and culminating in Sheffield United v Wolves on Sunday (12:00 BST).

title: No plans for Ireland Six Nations game in US - IRFU
description: There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.
fullText:
There are "currently no plans or discussions" relating to Ireland playing a Six Nations match in the United States, the Irish Rugby Football Union (IRFU) says.

World Rugby's chief executive Alan Gilpin said on Wednesday that it would help any nation that wants to switch a Six Nations match to the US, as it continues its drive to spread the game stateside.

He used the example of Ireland v Italy as a game that would resonate with expatriate fans in the United States and could help the sport further establish itself there.

But, in a statement issued on Friday, the IRFU dismissed the idea that it was considering moving any fixtures to the US.

"The United States is an important growth market for rugby and we welcome and embrace initiatives that help introduce the sport to new audiences and, crucially, generate new revenues for the game," said an IRFU spokesperson.

"There are currently no plans or discussions, from an IRFU perspective, regarding Six Nations matches being played in the United States.

"We believe the Six Nations holds a special place for supporters across all participating unions, and the opportunity for fans in Ireland and Italy to support their teams at home remains a central part of the competition's appeal."

Switch Six Nations fixture to USA to grow game – World Rugby

In an interview with the Daily Telegraph, external and The Times, external, Gilpin said: "This isn't a live discussion of an Italy v Ireland game, but why we use that as an example is because you've got two fantastic fanbases in the US of Irish and Italian fans.

"If you could take a Six Nations game to the right place, to a Boston or to a New York, where there's a lot of those fanbases, you can definitely drive the economics.

"Now, you're going to have Irish fans and Italian fans in those respective home countries saying: 'Hang on a minute, you know, we want to see our country play?'

"The counter-argument to that [is] it's still Irish and Italian fans getting the chance to watch their team, so they're just not the ones who live in Ireland and Italy on this occasion. But that's a balancing piece we've got to work through."

Ireland have previously enjoyed two well-attended games in the US against New Zealand.

They memorably beat the All Blacks for the first time when the teams met in front of a capacity 60,000-strong crowd at Chicago's Soldier Field in 2016, with a 2025 rematch which they lost also proving a similar commercial success.

title: Eggs, insults & a champion with a fake beard - Garcia and Benn face off
description: A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and taunted a composed  Conor Benn with a boiled egg before Saturday's WBC welterweight title fight.
fullText:
A performative Ryan Garcia shouted, repeatedly swore and even ate a boiled egg - while Briton Conor Benn kept his cool - during a peculiar news conference in Las Vegas.

American Garcia defends his WBC welterweight belt against 29-year-old Benn at the T-Mobile Arena on Saturday.

A fight week which had been relatively quiet finally came to life on Thursday - thanks largely to the unpredictable champion.

While Garcia, 28, bounced between insults, threats and jokes, Benn remained relatively composed.

Benn spoke instead about giving supporters "value for money" and refused to be drawn into many of his rival's taunts.

"All the talking, tweeting, typing and streaming is done - I'm ready to fight," Benn said, while inexplicably wearing a bullet-proof style vest.

Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia

Benn 'dragged down to pits of hell' by weight cut

'Bottling it' - Garcia no-show for first Benn face-off

Garcia is one of boxing's biggest social media stars, with more than 13 million Instagram followers.

He recently appeared on WWE's Monday Night Raw and it did not take long for the news conference to take on a similarly theatrical feel.

Minutes after taking his seat, Garcia reached into a bag, pulled out the egg, calmly peeled it and ate it whole.

"He has a lot of familiarity with eggs so I thought I'd eat some," Garcia said, as his opponent's father - Nigel Benn - shook his head.

It was a reference to Benn's two positive tests for clomifene in 2022 and the WBC's subsequent ruling that elevated consumption of eggs could provide a reasonable explanation.

Adding to the bizarre atmosphere, Garcia said his egg was a bit dry and would benefit from some honey.

Garcia has also served a doping suspension after testing positive for ostarine following his 2024 fight with Devin Haney. Both fighters have denied knowingly taking banned substances.

Before the face-off, security confiscated an egg Garcia had tucked into his pocket, potentially preventing a repeat of last year's incident when Chris Eubank Jr slapped Benn across the face with one.

Benn and Garcia had to be separated at their launch event in New York in July, but there was no repeat this time. As Garcia continued talking, Benn put a finger to his lips, smiled and eventually turned away and left the stage.

Thursday's news conference was held inside Saturday's fight venue, with one section of T-Mobile Arena curtained off for the crowd.

Fans had begun queuing more than an hour before the doors opened. It was not a Saul 'Canelo' Alvarez-sized crowd - and far from anything like the travelling support Ricky Hatton once brought to Las Vegas - but there was still a healthy turnout.

Small pockets of travelling British supporters made themselves heard, while Garcia received a much louder but mixed reception.

Garcia said Benn had "lit a fire" by questioning his Mexican heritage. Benn - who spent 12 years of his childhood living in Majorca - responded by speaking fluently in Spanish.

There was another dose of theatre when WBA 'Super' welterweight world champion Teofimo Lopez, disguised with a fake beard, stood among the crowd to ask a question before revealing himself to loud cheers.

Garcia also took aim at Benn's manager Keith Connolly's hairline before turning his attention to the challenger's weight.

Benn has not made the 10st 7lb welterweight limit for more than four years, having fought Chris Eubank Jr twice at middleweight.

Garcia suggested Benn could rehydrate to whatever weight he wanted after Friday's weigh-in but questioned whether his brain would recover sufficiently from the cut.

"[Garcia should] worry about himself," Benn replied. "He seems to have enough problems as it is.

"I don't look at him, I just worry about myself and don't cut corners. We'll see who makes weight tomorrow."

Garcia did eventually acknowledge much of the showmanship was just that.

"All this is noise, I've done my job and I'm the better fighter," he said. "This is fun but we know what to do."

But it did not take him long to slip back into entertainer mode. Even after Benn had left, Garcia remained on stage - flexing, shouting and playing to the crowd.

title: How 9/11 'shattered the guise of safety' for tennis' travelling circus
description: On Friday, the US Open will pause and remember the victims of the 9/11 terror attack that took place 25 years ago.
fullText:
The Arthur Ashe Stadium will glow light blue from dusk until dawn as the US Open marks the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

American flags will be flown at half-mast as New York remembers the 2,977 people who died when hijackers crashed passenger jets into the Twin Towers in Manhattan on that day in 2001.

That year's US Open had concluded just two days earlier, with Lleyton Hewitt winning the men's singles title.

American player James Blake had lost in the second round that year and was in Augusta, Georgia, on Tuesday, 11 September.

But the New York-born future world number four says the day "shattered the guise of safety" felt by Americans and many professional tennis players.

"It was something that I just couldn't believe could happen in the States," Blake told BBC Sport.

"I don't know if we were all naive, or living under the guise of safety and feeling that everything was going to be OK, but it kind of shattered that for a while.

"There was a lot of panic, at every level - whether it be from the highest of highs in the political world to the people on the ground, to everyone around Ground Zero."

US Open: Tennis remembers 9/11, 25 years on

Blake, who would later reach two US Open quarter-finals, was in Augusta for a sweat test, having struggled with cramp during the tournament.

His father, though, was still in New York, where he worked. With mobile phone networks overloaded, there was an uncomfortable wait to discover he was safe and well.

Blake was living in Florida at the time, and with planes grounded, took a hire car from Augusta back to Tampa.

His next tournament was in Hong Kong two weeks later, and he admits it was far from easy to board the plane.

"It was definitely scary because I think you get so isolated in tennis," he said.

"You feel like the little bubble you are in, where you are a kind of travelling circus, is normal.

"And then when you realise how restricted travel can be, it wakes you up a little bit to the reality and how quickly things can change.

"It felt like there was a safety net around you. We lived in a bit of a dream world where you are living your dream of playing a sport for a living, and that can all be taken away."

Many domestic sporting events were paused in the aftermath of the attacks, and the Ryder Cup - which had been due to take place at The Belfry in England later that month - was postponed by twelve months.

In Blake's view, the return of competitive sport helped enormously.

"I think that was one of the things that brought the country back," he said.

"Sports were stopped, but when they came back having [then President] George W Bush throwing out the first pitch at a Yankees game - I'm not a Yankees fan, and I can't say I was necessarily a George W Bush fan - I was almost in tears at that moment.

"It was special to have a sitting president [do that]. And it also signified we are back - we are going to have sports, we are going to continue on with our lives.

"The world seemed like it was back on track in a small way."

There is always a ceremony to mark the anniversary when the date falls during the US Open, and there will be a minute's silence before both of Friday's men's singles semi-finals.

Before the night session - and the all-American semi-final between Ben Shelton and Frances Tiafoe - a giant flag will be unfurled on court as R&B artist JoJo sings The Star-Spangled Banner.

"To me it's a really poignant moment," Blake added.

"The 2001 US Open, I remember so well. What would have happened if it happened two or three days earlier, and we were all still there?

"To be perfectly honest, a lot of times I feel playing the national anthem at smaller sporting events is unnecessary.

"But for the US Open, being such an international event and having it around 9/11, I I think it is a great moment.

"It gives you a chance to reflect."

title: 'I want to play for mum' – Arsenal's Cooney-Cross
description: Arsenal's Kyra Cooney-Cross is preparing to play at Emirates Stadium for the first time since losing her mum Jess to cancer, and explains how she has been facing up to her bereavement "one day at a time".
fullText:
Arsenal's Emirates Stadium will be full of noise when midfielder Kyra Cooney-Cross steps on to the pitch this Sunday to face Crystal Palace.

But there will be one important person missing from the crowd: her mother, Jess.

The Australia midfielder will play at the stadium for the first time since losing her mum to cancer two months ago. It is something she says she has been taking "one day at a time".

"I know mum would want me here playing and training," she told BBC Sport. "And I want to play for the fans as well, to say thank you to them.

"But it's mixed emotions. Game days are very emotional for me now. They mean a lot more. I would say I'm excited, but it's also going to be an emotional day.

"I want to play and I want to play for her as well and for the fans."

Cooney-Cross's mum was diagnosed with stage four cholangiocarcinoma, a rare and aggressive form of bile duct cancer, in January of this year.

She passed away seven months later, in July, at the age of just 45.

"She was a beautiful human and I want to carry her with me on and off the pitch," said Cooney-Cross.

The Australia international credits her mother's sacrifices for helping shape her football career.

She added: "Mum was a single mum of four girls. Growing up, she was driving me four times a week to train in Melbourne, an hour and a half each way. We barely had money for fuel. I don't even know half of the sacrifices she's made.

"I want to carry her in everything I do and how I am and how I play. Because she was honestly amazing."

Cooney-Cross, who is the eldest of four sisters, describes being told that her mum had terminal cancer just after Christmas as the moment her world changed "forever".

The phone call from her stepdad was made even more difficult by the fact she was in England at the time, having decided not to travel home for the holidays.

Upon hearing the diagnosis, the 24-year-old took the "next flight home" and an indefinite period of compassionate leave from football to spend her mother's final months by her side.

"That time at home was something I definitely needed. Being able to be at home and slow down, be present and being with my mum was the most important thing," she said.

"Being able to be there with her over the last six months and then that last week, it's sad, but I think we also need to think of it as a beautiful thing as well.

"My mum was truly something special."

Cooney-Cross is one of Australia's brightest stars. She broke into the international side at 19 and has made 63 appearances, starting all seven matches at the home World Cup in 2023.

She says continuing to train back home while spending time with her family was a welcome distraction from the emotional situation she was facing.

"I was training Monday to Friday on the pitch with a one-on-one coach and then I had a gym facility as well," she said.

"I did it because it was also an escape. I felt more free and like I could escape from everything that was going on off the pitch.

"I also did it because I knew that's what mum would want and I wanted to come back this season and be as fit as possible."

Returning to football after six months away from the game is a daunting prospect for any athlete, but the midfielder says Arsenal's care for her during her time away was "amazing".

Head coach Renee Slegers and director of women's football Claire Wheatley checked in regularly, while team-mates Alessia Russo and Taylor Hinds have also been huge emotional supports for her.

"That's when you need people and those that love you and care about you will be there for you," said Cooney-Cross.

"I was sad to leave my family, but at the same time, I also felt ready to come back. I had to bite the bullet. I'm so glad I did because honestly everyone has been so amazing.

"I've been distracted, I've been supported and it's been a really smooth transition. I've got good people around me."

Cooney-Cross was an unused substitute in Arsenal's opening game of the season against Brighton. The last time her mum saw her play football was at the Emirates, and the midfielder hopes to make her proud when she returns to the stadium this weekend.

"She was always the best at sending messages and I read this one [text] message before every game. The way she writes is so beautiful. I think a lot about how I go about life. I think about what she would say or do.

"A lot of my purpose is because of her and my drive, but even more so now. I just want to play and do really well for her and bring joy into the sadness of my family."

title: Saint-Maximin on speaking out after his children were racially abused
description:
Former Newcastle winger Allan Saint-Maximin says he felt it was important to
speak out after his children were racially abused earlier this year in Mexico.
fullText:
Allan Saint-Maximin could have stayed quiet.

But the French winger felt it was "important to step up" and speak out after his children were racially abused this year.

"Whatever your colour is, you don't have to accept this," he tells BBC Sport.

Saint-Maximin made it clear on Instagram in January that "hatred and discrimination have no place in our society".

The lengthy post was liked by more than 159,000 people, including former Newcastle United team-mates Kieran Trippier and Joelinton.

The father of four has not gone into specifics.

However, before returning to his homeland to play for Lens, he said "some stuff happened with my kids in the school" during his spell at Mexican side Club America.

"I explained to the kids what happened was not normal and they knew already," he says. "They were not really happy about that.

"I was a bit sad about my son, but in every place there is these type of things, even in France, the country where I am from. As I said to them, it's something they don't have to accept.

"After, when we moved to Lens, it was good but you see some stuff and you are like, 'in every place, there are some things different or some things you are not going to like'.

"If you are waiting for the perfect place, you are wrong."

Saint-Maximin leaves club over racist abuse of his children

Club America issued a statement expressing "absolute solidarity" with Saint-Maximin and his family, who had the "support of everyone who is part of this institution".

His team-mates held up a 'No to racism' banner before their game against Necaxa.

"It was not the fault of Club America," Saint-Maximin says. "I have nothing against them, the players or the Mexican people. I love the club. It was one of the best places I've been with my family.

"It's just some random people say some stuff and try to attack your family. You never really know who they support or why they do this, but when this affects your kids there are not many choices to take.

"It was a difficult choice for me and my family, but I take my responsibility because I always say I will never accept stuff like this.

"It was important to show to people, especially in my situation, that I can lose a lot of things, but I will never accept this."

Saint-Maximin joined Lens on a short-term deal in the second half of last season.

He played his part in Lens winning the French Cup for the first time in their 120-year history and finishing second in Ligue 1.

Saint-Maximin had a number of offers in the summer, but decided to move to Major League Soccer side Charlotte.

"My family have always followed me to every single place," he says. "So this time was more of a family choice.

"It was a way for me to give back what they have given to me since I started my career."

Saint-Maximin has linked up with former Aston Villa manager Dean Smith, a "straightforward guy" who is going to "tell you the truth straight away".

One of the club's two 'designated players',, external Saint-Maximin has set out to create a legacy under Smith and help those around him improve.

He also wants to entertain Charlotte supporters.

"To see some robot play doesn't make sense to me," the 29-year-old says.

Saint-Maximin is clearly anything but robotic.

The maverick proved something of a cult figure as Newcastle fought to stay in the Premier League for much of his time at the club.

Saint-Maximin also sampled the highs as a resurgent Newcastle qualified for the Champions League in his final campaign on Tyneside in 2023.

But he was only too aware that staff "could lose their jobs" if they went down.

"When you feel that opportunity, that feeling on your shoulder, you are like, 'this is heavy'," he says.

Saint-Maximin embraced that responsibility after quickly striking up a bond with Newcastle supporters following his move from Nice.

He volunteered at the city's foodbank and even gave fans gifts, including Rolex watches.

"If I was able to give all of my money to them, I would because there is nothing better than the feeling they give you," he adds. "It's something you can't buy, and I've tried to.

"The love they give to you, when I ran with the ball, I had the feeling of people behind me and I ran because of them.

"This feeling is incredible. I wish the same for every single player because they can bring the best out of you."

Saint-Maximin spent four years at Newcastle - the longest stint in his nomadic career - before joining Saudi Pro League side Al-Ahli.

He worked with Newcastle's current head coach, Matthias Jaissle, who took over from Eddie Howe this summer.

Saint-Maximin hopes the German and his staff "have the best possible time" at St James' Park - just as he did.

"Newcastle is my dream club," he says. "I love it from the bottom of my heart. I watch every single game.

"They gave me what no-one gave to me and I'll never forget that. I'm very loyal. I had many opportunities to come to the Premier League, but I didn't because of them."

title: West Ham's Alvarez denies kidnapping accusation
description: West Ham and Mexico midfielder Edson Alvarez posts a statement on social media denying the allegation made by film producer Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez.
fullText:
West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez has denied accusations he was involved in the alleged kidnapping of a film producer in Mexico.

Juan Jose Lopez Ordonez told Mexican publication TV Notas, external that he was forced into a vehicle at gunpoint in the Polanco district of Mexico City in 2024 by the family of Alvarez's former father-in-law Jonathan Toache Bedolla.

Ordonez, who claims Alvarez was not directly involved in the kidnapping but was aware of the plot, says he was commissioned to make a documentary about the footballer's life and was owed £150,000 for the project.

Alvarez, who made his Mexico debut in 2017, issued a statement on his social media to deny the allegations and says he will consider legal action.

"I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me," Alvarez, who is also Mexico's captain, posted on social media.

"Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.

"Until now, I had chosen not to respond. However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line."

He added that the media outlets were prioritising "sensationalism" instead of "accuracy and truth" and said he would keep focusing on his family and his career.

Alvarez has made 74 appearances for the Hammers since joining from Ajax in 2023, but has only featured once so far this season, against Portsmouth in the Carabao Cup.

title: Rybakina sets up blockbuster Sabalenka final at US Open
description: Soon-to-be world number one Elena Rybakina will face Aryna Sabalenka in a blockbuster US Open final between the tournament's top two seeds.
fullText:
Soon-to-be world number one Elena Rybakina produced a gritty comeback against Coco Gauff to reach the US Open final, in which she will face Aryna Sabalenka in a blockbuster showdown between the tournament's top two seeds.

Rybakina is guaranteed to end Sabalenka's 99-week reign as world number one and will replace the Belarusian at the top when the rankings are updated on Monday.

But the Kazakh second seed could rub more salt in Sabalenka's wounds if she can deny the top seed a third successive US Open title in Saturday's showpiece.

Sabalenka sent a warning to her rivals as she overpowered home hope Jessica Pegula 7-5 6-2 to keep alive her bid to become the third woman in the Open era to win the New York singles title three times in a row.

Rybakina will stand in her way after she fought back to beat American fourth seed Gauff 3-6 6-4 6-4 and silence the partisan crowd.

"I took a deep breath and just told myself I needed to fight and show good tennis," Rybakina said.

The 27-year-old is chasing her third Grand Slam title after winning Wimbledon in 2022 and beating Sabalenka in January's Australian Open final.

It will be the first time the top two women's seeds have contested a US Open final since Serena Williams beat Victoria Azarenka in the 2013 showpiece.

Sabalenka has not been beaten in New York since losing the 2023 final to Gauff, but there were doubts over her title defence following a poor run-up to the tournament.

After a strong start to the season and winning the 'Sunshine Double' at Indian Wells and Miami in March, Sabalenka suffered a quarter-final defeat at Roland Garros and a fourth-round exit at Wimbledon.

However, she has found her form again, dropping just one set en route to the final.

"I was super desperate," Sabalenka said after her win over Pegula.

"It feels for me, talking about Grand Slams, like a last push of the season.

"I wanted it badly to go to the finals, and of course, I want to go all the way."

In a tense opening set, Sabalenka bristled with frustration early on as unforced errors crept into her game while Pegula settled quickly and struck the ball cleanly.

But eventually the four-time major singles winner found her rhythm and, after striking decisively at 6-5 to take the first set, she cranked up the power.

Pegula looked helpless as Sabalenka raced through the second set, with the Belarusian pounding 29 winners to her 12.

The victory meant Sabalenka broke the Open era record for the most Grand Slam hard-court finals in a row, with the 28-year-old reaching every major final on her favoured surface since the 2023 Australian Open.

For 32-year-old Pegula - the only semi-finalist without a Grand Slam title - it is yet another US Open defeat by long-time rival Sabalenka.

Sabalenka denied the third seed a maiden major in the 2024 final, while she also got the better of her in last year's semi-finals - although Pegula had won their most recent meeting in June's Berlin Open.

"I do think she probably would have beaten 99% of people," Pegula said.

"Probably the best match she's played this year."

Hewett & Reid into men's wheelchair doubles final

Listen: US Open - tennis remembers 9/11 25 years on

Rybakina's ascent to the top of the world rankings is already assured but she has made it clear that for all the prestige of being number one, winning titles is what she really cares about.

"It's just a number right now, my goal is to win the tournaments which I play," the 27-year-old said before her semi-final.

A three-set victory over Gauff showed all of Rybakina's resilience and ability to absorb a setback - coming from a set down and then being broken when serving for the match - before striking back.

But for much of the match, she was well short of her destructive best.

"I definitely need to step my game up [in the final], serve better than today, stay aggressive and really go for my shots," the two-time major winner added.

The prospect of a final between the top two seeds is tantalising enough but that it is the outgoing number one taking on her successor makes it all the more mouth-watering.

While Sabalenka holds the edge in the head-to-head with 10 wins in 17 meetings, including beating Rybakina in the semi-finals in Miami and the final at Indian Wells this year, the Kazakh came out on top when they met in January's Australian Open final.

Sabalenka led 3-0 in the deciding set in Melbourne but eventually fell to a third defeat in her past four Grand Slam finals.

Meanwhile, Rybakina's only loss in three previous major finals was to Sabalenka in Australia in 2023.

title: Why Nigel Benn can't walk away from Conor
description: Nigel Benn vowed to leave son Conor to plough his own path after he beat Chris Eubank Jr, but the retired world champion is back by his side this week as he prepares to face WBC welterweight champion Ryan Garcia.
fullText:
Nigel Benn had insisted he was stepping away from his son's career for good.

The 10,000-mile trips from Australia - where Nigel is based - were done, and Conor Benn was on his own after his grudge-match win over Chris Eubank Jr.

Yet in the build-up to Conor's WBC welterweight world title challenge against Ryan Garcia in Las Vegas, the 'Dark Destroyer' was by his son's side at the news conference and holding court at their Essex media day - as embedded as ever.

Ask Nigel why and he claims Conor "twisted my arm" into helping with one final hurdle.

"I don't know if he was lying or if he believed it himself," Conor says with a wry smile.

"He lives through me. He goes, 'son, this is my last fight, I'm done.' Then the next one it's, 'son, it's your first defence.' There'll always be something."

Perhaps neither man is ready to cut the cord.

Conor has stepped out of his 62-year-old father's shadow - not by matching the legendary ring achievements, but through the sheer turbulence of his own journey.

Navigating a career-threatening doping case, surviving the ferocious Eubank rivalry and acrimoniously splitting from long-time promoter Eddie Hearn transformed him from 'Nigel's boy' into one of British boxing's most polarising headliners.

Through those storms, Nigel has been there in the trenches.

"It's what Conor thinks and what his dad thinks - that's what it's about, not what everybody else says," Nigel Benn says.

"Everyone's not going to love my son. Everybody didn't love me. But once you get that belt around his waist, we'll go from there."

Thirty-six years ago, Nigel flew across the Atlantic as the fiery outsider, tearing through Doug DeWitt in Atlantic City to secure his first world title.

Now, Conor lands on the Las Vegas Strip chasing the exact same milestone. A victory would place the Benns alongside the likes of Floyd and Tracy Harris Patterson, Julio Cesar Chavez and Julio Cesar Chavez Jr and Leon and Cory Spinks in the lineage of father-and-son world champions.

"I've watched him religiously for 10 years put his life on the line," Nigel says. "He's just going from strength to strength, from glory to glory. I see him being victorious. I'm not actually worried whatsoever."

Yet reaching this point has required navigating a volatile road fraught with controversy.

The adverse drug test findings that wiped out two years of Conor's career cast a long shadow, fracturing public perception and leaving unanswered questions that still follow him.

He has always denied doping, a provisional suspension was lifted in November 2024, and he says he has fought throughout his career as "an advocate for clean sport".

Inside the ropes, the jury remains stubbornly out on his talent.

A laboured points victory over Regis Prograis in his last outing did little to convince purists he belongs at the sport's highest echelon.

But Conor cares little for the outside noise or winning over the boxing fraternity.

"To some people, I'll never be good enough," he says. "One day they love you, some day they hate you.

"You keep talking about what other people think, but I don't care. Winning the world title for me, it's personal. If I listen to other people, I wouldn't be where I am."

'Bottling it' - Garcia no-show for first Benn face-off

Benn does not deserve world title shot - Garcia

Benn 'dragged down to pits of hell' by weight cut

Garcia has walked an equally chaotic path, having served a one-year suspension after testing positive for banned substance ostarine following his win over Devin Haney in 2024.

Both men deny intentionally ever taking performance-enhancing drugs, but away from that issue their showdown is wrapped in the contradictions that define modern boxing.

It will be staged by UFC-backed Zuffa Boxing - following Conor's high-profile split from Hearn - yet featuring the traditional green-and-gold WBC belt on the line, despite Zuffa's public rhetoric about disrupting boxing's old-guard sanctioning bodies.

Social media spats between the fighters have brought plenty of heat, but Conor Benn does not compare it to the raw nature of the Eubank saga, which spilled over into face-to-face fury. An egg was even slapped across Benn's face by Eubank.

"Listen, it's not personal with Ryan. It is personal with Eubank - this ain't no comparison," Conor says.

"One person I wanted to put in hospital; the other one I don't. I just want his title and I want his number one position. I've been at world level for years and for me to claim the number one spot officially is the goal here.

"[Garcia] is like a child. It doesn't bother me. You need people like Ryan in the sport of boxing."

Garcia is proven at the top level and enters as the favourite, bringing blinding hand speed and a fight-ending left hook.

But Nigel Benn believes he has mapped out the exact antidote to Garcia's firepower. He says his son should attack Garcia using suffocating, bobbing aggression - the kind that Nigel used to blow out Iran Barkley in 1990.

"When he goes under pressure, what happens? He falls and his heart doesn't go into it," Nigel says.

"For the first time, [Conor] is actually sitting there listening. He has to be not the destroyer, he has to be the Dark Destroyer. Controlled aggression.

"Don't give him room. Roll under his punches, left hook to the body, left hook to the head. He knows what to do."

The hostile Vegas spotlight, meanwhile, evokes memories of Benn senior's ferocious 1995 battle with Gerald McClellan.

"Everybody had me to be blown out within round three. Exactly the same thing as what they do with Conor," Nigel says. "And I know he's going to prevail."

Win, lose or draw, Nigel insists this time he will walk away for good and let Conor do his own thing.

"I can walk out of that arena, go home, and be with my family, and that's it," Nigel says.

Whether Nigel finally catches that one-way flight back to Sydney is another matter.

If Conor leaves Las Vegas with the WBC belt around his waist, you would not bet against his father being back for defence number one.

title: Leeds want boss Farke to stay 'long-term'
description: Leeds United managing director Robbie Evans says the club and boss Daniel Farke are "on the same page" as they look to agree a new contract.
fullText:
Leeds United managing director Robbie Evans says the club and boss Daniel Farke are "on the same page" as they look to agree a new contract.

Farke, who guided Leeds to a 14th-placed finish in the Premier League and an FA Cup semi-final last season after winning promotion in 2024-25, is in the final year of his current deal.

The Whites have taken five points from three league games this campaign and Evans said the German had done "a fantastic job".

"As far as the contract discussions themselves, Daniel and his team and I have had really good chats for the past three months and they're all on the same page," he said.

"Unlike signing him back in 2023 or doing a deadline day deal kind of thing the time pressure is far reduced and so we have a time to get it right as far as what he wants and what we want.

"I don't feel it's taking a long time. It just means we're getting it right and also we have time to get it right and so as long as we're still operating together as a group, and we're doing great on that front, I'm not worried."

He added: "The the short answer is that he's done great, we want him to be here long-term and we're working on it."

Leeds brought in England goalkeeper James Trafford from Manchester City in a deal worth up to £45m in the summer, as well as defenders Tarik Muharemovic and Nico Elvedi and Fulham winger Harry Wilson.

They also added Nice defender Melvin Bard and Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jean-Matteo Bahoya on deadline day.

"I think last year the phrase was we had a good window and a bad deadline. I would say this summer was a good window and a good deadline," Evans said.

"The key for us was we had a couple of top objectives to accomplish and those all got done early in terms of a left-footed centre-half, right winger and goalkeeper. Having signed our top targets in all three of those positions we were able to go and pursue roles around the pitch that gets better and stronger and have time to do so.

"So we're quite satisfied with the window."

Netherlands international Pascal Struijk was sold to Brighton in a deal worth a reported £20m on 30 June.

The last day of June is when clubs needed to be compliant with profit and sustainability rules (PSR) to avoid charges and possible points deductions. This is now being replaced by squad-cost ratio (SCR) moving forward.

Evans said he was "thankful" the club only needed to sell one player in order to come into line with the regulations.

"I was pretty confident coming into the year we'd have to sell some guys in June. Frankly it was the FA Cup run and the minimal work in January that kept it being just one player," he said.

"Pascal's appeal to other teams was clear before the year was over and then he was debating going or not and he was helpful in deciding pretty quickly so we could decide to sell him before 30 June.

"We were prepared for that possibility all season and so we did tonnes of work on a left centre-half last year. Having that news early was helpful, but we had, like always, various contingencies for Pascal."

title: More than 100,000 watch 49ers shock Rams in Melbourne
description: San Francisco 49ers record dominant 27-7 victory over Super Bowl favourites Los Angeles Rams in front of a crowd of more than 100,000 at Melbourne Cricket Ground.
fullText:
San Francisco 49ers recorded a dominant 27-7 victory over Super Bowl favourites Los Angeles Rams in front of a crowd of more than 100,000 at Melbourne Cricket Ground.

It was the NFL's first game in the Asia-Pacific region, and its longest-ever road trip for the first of a record nine international games in 2026.

The 49ers arrived in Melbourne a week before the game, while the Rams opted to spend just over 24 hours in Australia.

Sean McVay's side are Super Bowl favourites after acquiring defensive end Myles Garrett and welcoming one of the NFL's greatest defensive players, Aaron Donald, out of retirement.

"I love when they [the Rams] came out and they were booing. We were out here for a week. We enjoyed the city. I don't think you can fly 16 hours and be ready to play," 49ers receiver Deebo Samuel told Australia's Channel Seven.

The game came to life in the second quarter as Kyren Williams ran in for a touchdown to give the Rams a four-point advantage following an earlier 49ers field goal.

However, the 49ers hit back as Demarcus Robinson grabbed a touchdown before half-time.

The momentum continued as receiver Mike Evans scored, followed by a touchdown from Samuel - and a second field goal sealed the win for the 49ers.

Quarterback Brock Purdy completed 25 of 34 passes for 205 yards, including three touchdown passes.

McVay added: "I make no excuses. Whether you want to say it's about travel, whatever. We just weren't good enough.

"I didn't coach good enough, and we'll look at it and we'll move forward."

title: Hall signs new contract with Newcastle until 2031
description: Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall signs a new contract with the club that runs until 2031.
fullText:
Newcastle United defender Lewis Hall has signed a new contract with the club that runs until 2031.

The left-back, who has been the subject of interest from Manchester United, has agreed a two-year extension to his original deal.

Hall said it was a "really proud moment" to extend his stay as a boyhood supporter of the club.

"It's an absolute pleasure to play for this club and to represent the supporters," he said. "I know how much it means to them.

"To be able to bring joy to their faces, it's a big thing for me. I obviously have a family connection with the club, which is incredibly important to us all.

"One of the main reasons I play is to make my family proud, and I know how much it means to them to watch me playing for Newcastle United.

"It's a really good place to be. It's really pleasing with how we've started the season, especially with the new gaffer [Matthias Jaissle] and coaching staff coming in, and I think we can go on to achieve really big things."

Hall, 22, has made 106 appearances for Newcastle since joining the club from Chelsea in 2023.

Jaissle said the defender is a "very important player for us and for what we are building here".

"His mentality is exactly what you want in a young player," he said. "He wants to learn every day and he wants to be better in every match.

"Lewis covers ground in a way that few players can. He defends with maturity and intelligence, and his technical level means he can support the team higher up the pitch.

"What excites me most is that I believe the best is still to come from Lewis. He has a lot of room to develop, and I am looking forward to working with him as he grows with us."

This has been a busy summer at Newcastle - both in terms of ins and outs - but tying Hall down is a particularly significant move.

It was just last month that Jaissle replied "no chance" when Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel informed him that his former side were looking at Hall.

This deal further strengthens the club's position.

It also rewards Hall for his development since he arrived from Chelsea as a raw left-back three years ago.

Hall has worked on the defensive side of his game and, on his day, proved he is capable of even keeping Barcelona star Lamine Yamal quiet from open play in the Champions League.

He has been a real outlet going forward for Newcastle, too, and has already set up two goals this season.

That should not come as a huge surprise.

Of those full-backs to play a minimum of 900 minutes across the Premier League last season, Hall led the way for high-speed runs and underlapping runs per game. He also ranked in the top three for dribbles completed per match.

It feels like there is a lot more to come from him as he looks to get back into the England squad after missing out on the World Cup.
